arguments.value: 43-year-old man with weakness, constipation, dry skin, leukopenia/anemia, and cellulitis was evaluated for hypothyroidism after outside concern for dermatomyositis/anti-synthetase syndrome due to hand and finger-joint skin changes. He was found to have markedly elevated TSH with low free thyroxine, abdominal distension with severe constipation, and a left leg subcutaneous abscess growing methicillin-sensitive Staphylococcus aureus. Further history revealed heavy tororo kombu intake, leading to a diagnosis of iodine-induced hypothyroidism; thyroid hormone replacement and restriction of iodine-rich foods improved his thyroid function, skin findings, symptoms, and blood counts.
